mappings.mapping_description: MAESTRO directly addresses EO-01 through two integrated research pillars and a cross-cutting capability. Pillar 1 (Neuro-Symbolic Planning and Reasoning) develops a hybrid planning engine that decomposes high-level goals into formally verifiable sub-task graphs with monitoring and self-correction, delivering improvements in autonomy and reliability not achievable by pure LLM-based approaches. Pillar 2 (Adaptive Memory Architecture) designs a unified working/episodic/semantic memory system with a memory controller managing information flow across stores, enabling coherent long-horizon agent behaviour and directly addressing memory management. The External Tool and API Orchestration Layer provides post-invocation verification, grounding in verified external data, and execution monitoring with fallback/recovery, directly enhancing agent robustness and reliability. All three elements collectively produce significant improvements in autonomy, robustness, and reliability through advanced planning, memory management, and reasoning capabilities as required by EO-01.

mappings.mapping_description: MAESTRO directly addresses EO-02 through Pillar 3 (Decentralised Multi-Agent Coordination). The concept develops: (1) a formal task-delegation protocol where agents decompose tasks, negotiate subtask assignments, and establish shared commitment structures with provable convergence guarantees; (2) conflict resolution mechanisms for plan interference, contested resources, and inconsistent world models; and (3) fully auditable delegation and negotiation traces that humans can inspect. The External Tool and API Orchestration Layer extends multi-agent capability by governing shared tool access, delegated tool invocation, and conflict resolution when multiple agents require the same external resource. This constitutes an innovative multi-agent framework demonstrating effective decentralised coordination and collaboration among multiple heterogeneous AI agents with capabilities beyond individual agents.
